summary: The profile shows no leakage suspects, no fields with heavy missing data and no constant features. All six candidate features (leverage, interest_coverage, current_ratio, log_assets, profit_margin and sector) look like standard origination financials, so I recommend keeping them all. The main concerns are a small number of default events and a design that has not been specified: the horizon, default definition, use case and segment are all blank and need sponsor confirmation. Vintage should stay in the dataset for the out-of-time split but should not be used as a model input.

column_decisions.reason: Not recommended as a model input, and it is already outside the feature list. It is kept in the dataset only because the out-of-time vintage split needs it, and excluding it would remove it from every downstream stage.
This is the strongest single correlate of default, but at a plausible level well below the leakage threshold. As a balance-sheet ratio, it is normally known at origination.

data_quality.statement: The observed default rate is above the typical 1-5% annual range for commercial portfolios, though below the level that would suggest a mislabeled flag. It should be reconciled with the sponsor's default definition and horizon.

The sample has few default events relative to 6 features, including a categorical sector field. Estimates by sector level and by vintage will be noisy, and the out-of-time holdout will reduce the events further.
The engine flagged no feature as a leakage suspect. All absolute correlations with default are modest, the largest being leverage.

Profit margin has almost no linear correlation with default. It may be weak on its own, have a non-linear relationship, or contain spreading or unit errors, so it is worth checking against the -35% to +45% sanity range.

questions_for_sponsor: What is the default definition (for example 90+ DPD, nonaccrual, bankruptcy or charge-off), and over what horizon is it measured (for example 12 months from origination)?
Is the score used at origination or at a periodic surveillance snapshot? Are the financial ratios taken from the statement available at that date, rather than one spread afterwards?
Are the most recent vintages fully seasoned for the default horizon, or are they right-censored?
Which segment does the model cover (for example middle market or small business), and should sector be modeled as-is or grouped?
Are leverage and interest_coverage defined in the usual way (Debt/EBITDA and EBIT/interest), and is profit_margin stated as a fraction or as a percentage?
uncertainties: The profile gives no distribution statistics (min, max or percentiles), so I could not check the ratios against their sanity ranges or look for spreading or unit errors.
The timing of the financial fields relative to the prediction date is not documented, so the absence of leakage rests only on correlation levels and column names.
The default count is small, so any conclusion about individual features, sector levels or vintage stability rests on thin evidence.
